text:
evan: heads-up: the example app we ship in the edge starter is confusing users — when imported from a Next/Nodenext project the exported generics are showing up as `any`. file an FYI here before i open a PR.

jin: ouch. is that only when the consumer builds for ESM? or also plain Node ESM?

ev an: only for ESM consumers (vite/next with nodenext). CJS consumers see the overloads fine. seems related to how editors/resolvers pick .d.ts for the conditional export.

tess: do you have package.json exports and the `types` entry handy? sometimes TS will prefer a `*.mjs.d.ts` file if present.

ovar: (typo) omar: i saved a tiny repro — simpler than our code:
```ts
// src/lib.ts
export function wrap(x: string): string;
export function wrap<T>(x: T): T;
export function wrap(x: any) { return x }
```
builds to dist/esm/index.mjs + dist/cjs/index.cjs and a single dist/index.d.ts. in ESM consumers the IDE shows wrap as `(x: any) => any`.

jin: probable cause: Node's resolution for conditional exports does not consult the package `types` or the plain index.d.ts the way you'd expect for ESM imports. TS chooses a `types` path using `exports` map or typesVersions. if your ESM entry points to a file with a different name, tsc/vite may look for `index.mjs.d.ts` and fallback to `any` if missing.

ev an: got it. so options: 1) produce index.mjs.d.ts alongside ESM entry, 2) add `typesVersions` to map ESM imports to our flat d.ts, or 3) point `types` to a neutral path under dist that both import/require resolve to.

tess: also check your tsconfig: if the package is published with `module: nodenext` we recommend `moduleResolution: bundler` for editor perf, but that changes lookup semantics. we have seen `moduleResolution: node` and `bundler` behave differently for extensionless imports.

omar: another twist: bundlers (esbuild/tsup/rollup) sometimes post-process types and collapse overloads if the implementation signature is `any` or uses `unknown` inconsistently. replacing the implementation signature with a constrained generic keeps declaration emit stable: `function wrap<Z>(x: Z): Z { return x as Z }` instead of `any`.

jin: +1. and avoid writing the implementation with reassigned `any` variables that leak to the d.ts via type widening. if you must use `any` inside, prefer to cast only at the boundary: `return x as unknown as Z`.

type-checker-bot: note: CI type-check job failed once for starter when ESM consumers got `any`. adding a tsd test prevented regressions.

tess: what's our recommended starter fix? i can open a small change to the build pipeline.

ev an: patch i tried locally: emit declarations to `dist/types/index.d.ts`, copy that file to `dist/esm/index.mjs.d.ts` and `dist/cjs/index.cjs.d.ts` as part of postbuild. update package.json: keep `types` pointing at `dist/types/index.d.ts` and add `typesVersions` mapping `*` to `dist/types/*`.

omar: that worked in my quick test. IDE picks up overloads and tsserver shows the right signatures. downside is slightly bigger package and extra copy step, but negligible.

jin: can we avoid copies by making exports point to a neutral `dist/index.js` that re-exports both ESM and CJS? that might be more invasive.

tess: for DX, let's do the postbuild copy + add a tiny tsd test that imports from `dist/esm` and asserts types for a sample generic function. add a short note to the starter README explaining nodenext vs bundler lookup and `typesVersions` mention.

ev an: i'll open PR with postbuild script + tsd CI job. also include a comment in package.json explaining why `types` is pinned to dist/types.

omar: while we're at it, maybe add a troubleshooting snippet to the contributor docs showing how to reproduce the failing symptom locally (example consumer repo with nodenext config). saves folks time.

jin: and remind maintainers to avoid implementation-level `any` in public exports. small lint rule? `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` with an allowlist for internal tests could help.

type-checker-bot: created issue #499: "starter: ESM consumers get collapsed overloads / any in editor" and linked PR starter/fix-esm-types-499.

ev an: thanks everyone. once PR is up i'll ping eng-devex for review.

tess: nice work. quick checklist for the PR message: explain root cause, describe postbuild copy, show small tsd assertion, and add README note. :thumbsup:
